items.title: Musk's political baggage clouds prospects for SpaceX-Tesla deal
items.author: Cassell Bryan-Low, Hyunjoo Jin
items.creator: Cassell Bryan-Low, Hyunjoo Jin
items.summary: The possible merger may face bigger obstacles from politics than from regulation, drawing scrutiny in Beijing and potentially igniting a battle between President Donald Trump and the Democrats.
items.body:
A possible merger between Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX (SPCX.O) and carmaker Tesla (TSLA.O) may face bigger obstacles from politics than from regulation, drawing scrutiny in Beijing and potentially igniting a battle between US President Donald Trump and the Democrats.
Musk revived speculation about [USN:L4N4661IU TEXT:"a tie-up"] this week, calling a combination "a good idea" and confirming that committees at both companies were reviewing a potential deal, a step toward what could become the largest merger in history and create a company worth about $3.5 trillion.
But a merger would also unite one of the US government's most important aerospace and defense contractors with one of the most China-exposed major American manufacturers — a combination likely to raise questions about national security risks both in Washington and in Beijing.
Those concerns are unlikely to derail a deal, analysts said, but they would likely leave the combined company exposed to years of political wrangling and pressure from both sides of the Pacific.
Tesla's China operations, they said, could become a source of leverage for Beijing in any future dispute with Washington, while a Democratic takeover of the US House of Representatives in next month's midterm elections could subject the deal to congressional investigations and political maneuvering.
Democrats immediately raised concerns about the deal's implications, signaling their intent to turn the merger into a political flashpoint ahead of the November 3 midterms.
“If Elon Musk moves forward with the merger of Tesla and SpaceX, the deal would carry real risks that antitrust enforcers across the world would scrutinize," said US Senator Cory Booker, a New Jersey Democrat who sits on both the Judiciary and Foreign Relations committees.
He added that he was prepared to conduct oversight of any deal: "When one person controls the infrastructure that governments and militaries depend on, his business decisions become national security decisions, too."
Musk could seek to address concerns by limiting how closely the two companies are integrated.
The greater threat to the deal may come later, however, if a future administration takes a harder line on the relationship between Tesla and a company increasingly tied to US national security, analysts said.
"A merger agreement would involve pledges of limits to the connections between SpaceX and Tesla," said Derek Scissors, a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute.
"I don't think the Trump administration would enforce these limits. However, the next administration could certainly begin to scrutinize a merged entity. This may be the biggest risk to a deal - that it could get unwound in 2029."
EXPOSURE TO CHINA For Beijing, a merger would effectively place Tesla's sprawling Shanghai manufacturing hub under the same corporate umbrella as SpaceX, a company that has become deeply embedded in US military and national security activities through its Pentagon work and through Starlink's role in conflicts, including Ukraine.
"A formal merger would make it harder for Chinese authorities to treat Tesla as a purely commercial actor, raising risks for future factory expansions, data approvals, or market access," said Alicia Garcia-Herrero, a senior research fellow at the Brussels-based Bruegel think tank.
Tesla's reliance on production from Shanghai already gives China considerable leverage over Musk's business empire. A merger could extend that control to a broader corporate group encompassing strategically important assets such as satellite communications, launch services and military-related technologies.
GLOBAL REGULATORY HURDLES The deal would also have to navigate a maze of reviews around the world as competition authorities assess its impact on industries ranging from automobiles and satellite communications to artificial intelligence and semiconductors.
Musk's close relationship with Trump would likely dispel concerns about potential US regulatory roadblocks to a transaction, analysts said, while antitrust experts see limited competition concerns because the companies operate largely in separate markets.
Outside the United States, however, foreign regulators are likely to scrutinize whether a combined company would gain an unfair advantage by integrating technologies spanning automobiles, artificial intelligence and aerospace.
Antitrust experts said authorities in markets with powerful domestic auto industries, such as China and South Korea, could examine whether Tesla's access to SpaceX technologies would give it an advantage that rivals cannot replicate, creating barriers for competitors and potentially undermining domestic manufacturers.
Regulators could respond by requiring the company to license key technologies to competitors as part of any approval, said Ioannis Kokkoris, a law professor at Queen Mary University of London.
A South Korean antitrust official told Reuters that the merger, if pursued, could require an in-depth review of its potential impact on that country's industries.
"Korean antitrust officials will be wary of the merger. They will take the merger very seriously," said Lee Hwang, a law professor at Korea University and former Korea Fair Trade Commission official.
"The stakes are very high in Korea because it regards both the automotive and aerospace sectors as strategically important industries."
items.raw_description: The possible merger may face bigger obstacles from politics than from regulation, drawing scrutiny in Beijing and potentially igniting a battle between President Donald Trump and the Democrats.

items.title: Meta has strong chance of getting $25 billion New Mexico penalty slashed on appeal, experts say
items.author: Dietrich Knauth, Diana Jones
items.creator: Dietrich Knauth, Diana Jones
items.summary: Meta Platforms has a strong basis for arguing that the $25 billion penalty New Mexico secured this week in a case stemming from allegations the firm mishandled user data should be reduced on appeal, legal experts said.
items.body:
Meta Platforms (META.O) has a strong basis for arguing that the [USN:L6N46716L TEXT:"$25 billion penalty"] New Mexico secured this week in a case stemming from allegations the firm mishandled user data should be reduced on appeal, legal experts said.
The judgment was one of the largest state verdicts against a company in US history. It came after [USN:L6N46716L TEXT:"a jury found"] Meta misled consumers about who had access to their data in the wake of revelations that Cambridge Analytica, a political consulting firm involved in President Donald Trump 's 2016 presidential campaign, had harvested personal data from millions of Facebook users.
New Mexico said state law allowed for a penalty of up to $5,000 for each time someone in the state may have seen an allegedly misleading statement from Meta. Experts said the company would likely argue that Judge Francis Mathew should only have considered people who actually saw the statements.
"The most vulnerable basis on appeal is going to be the question about whether a violation is going to count, even in the absence of any proof that a particular person saw one of these misrepresentations or relied on them to their detriment," said Peter Ormerod, a law professor at Villanova University.
C.J. Mahoney, Meta's chief legal officer, said the company is confident it will win on appeal. The company is expected to appeal the underlying jury verdict and the penalty.
Meta has previously said that it does not sell user data and that New Mexico did not prove any consumer had actually been misled and that a penalty in the billions of dollars would risk violating its constitutional rights to due process and protection from excessive fines.
New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said on Wednesday he expected Meta to appeal the judgment and the state stood ready to defend its legal position. He did not immediately respond to a request for further comment.
JURY FOUND 43 MILLION VIOLATIONS New Mexico's attorney general sued Meta in 2021, alleging that the company lied to Facebook users about who had access to their data, how the company handled hate speech and misinformation posted on the platform, and other internal policies.
Jurors on September 25 found that 26 of 29 statements made by the company and its leadership on those issues were misleading. Multiplying those statements by their potential audience within New Mexico, the jury said the company had committed more than 43 million violations of the state’s consumer protection laws. The state had 1.4 million active Facebook users and a population of 2.1 million as of 2020.
Mathew said in his ruling on Wednesday that a penalty of more than $219 billion would be justified under state law, which allows a $5,000 penalty for each violation, but he reduced the amount.
The state had urged Mathew to award the state between $35 billion and $40 billion, while Meta said penalties of no more than $3.45 billion were warranted.
Ormerod said that even if the company's appeals in state courts fail, Meta could argue to the US Supreme Court that the penalty violated its rights under the US Constitution to due process and against excessive fines.
The size of the penalty on its own does not mean it will be overturned, given the New Mexico law allowing for penalties for each willful violation, said Daryl Lim, a professor at Penn State Dickinson Law.
But it seems implausible that Meta was really responsible for so much financial harm, a sign the penalty may be unjust, said Eric Goldman, a professor at Santa Clara University School of Law.
"It felt like there was a lot of duplicative counting in the calculations," Goldman said. "How many times can a single person be duped by the same entity?"
items.raw_description: Meta Platforms has a strong basis for arguing that the $25 billion penalty New Mexico secured this week in a case stemming from allegations the firm mishandled user data should be reduced on appeal, legal experts said.

items.title: Spotify forecasts fourth-quarter profit above estimates on AI bets
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Spotify forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates on Thursday, as the Swedish music streaming company bets on its AI-powered features to drive user growth in the crucial holiday season.
items.body:
Spotify (SPOT.N) forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates on Thursday, as the Swedish music streaming company bets on its AI-powered features to drive user growth in the crucial holiday season.
The company expects operating income of €820 million ($920.53 million), compared with analysts' average estimate of €813.4 million, according to data compiled by LSEG.
Shares of the company were last up more than 3% in volatile premarket trading.
Spotify offers AI-powered features such as its AI DJ, which curates personalized music mixes with spoken commentary, and prompt-based playlists that let users describe a mood or listening preference to generate tailored selections.
Investors closely monitor the company's profitability as it invests in AI to improve discovery and engagement on the platform to attract more users and fend off emerging music-generation rivals such as Suno and Udio.
In the third quarter, the company reported operating income of €672 million, in line with Visible Alpha-compiled analysts' average estimate of €671.8 million.
Spotify reported revenue of €4.97 billion in the quarter, compared with estimates of €4.98 billion, according to LSEG data.
"This was a quarter where we did what we said. We've built a strong business that keeps compounding, we invest when we see a path for growth, our costs are moderating, and there is more runway ahead," co-CEO Alex Norstrom said in a statement.
Spotify's monthly active users forecast of 818 million for the fourth quarter was marginally below Visible Alpha estimates of 819 million, while its outlook for a 10 million increase in premium subscribers to 316 million was above estimates of 314.7 million.
($1 = 0.8908 euros)
items.raw_description: Spotify forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates on Thursday, as the Swedish music streaming company bets on its AI-powered features to drive user growth in the crucial holiday season.

items.title: US Supreme Court rulings reshape midterm election battlefield
items.author: John Kruzel
items.creator: John Kruzel
items.summary: The November 3 midterm elections are quickly approaching after an electoral cycle shaped to an unusual degree by decisions of the US Supreme Court, a development that prompted Justice Elena Kagan to voice alarm this week.
items.body:
The November 3 midterm elections are quickly approaching after an electoral cycle shaped to an unusual degree by decisions of the US Supreme Court , a development that prompted Justice Elena Kagan to [USN:L1N46700J TEXT:"voice alarm"] this week.
Republicans generally have fared better than Democrats in the spate of recent election-related cases, including in rulings on redrawing congressional districts and rolling back campaign finance restrictions. It remains to be seen, however, whether these [USN:L1N4660I0 TEXT:"legal victories will help"] President Donald Trump 's party in its quest to retain control of Congress in the midterms.
Democrats need a net gain of four seats each in the House of Representatives and Senate to overcome narrow Republican majorities in those chambers. Ceding control of either chamber to the Democrats would endanger Trump's legislative agenda and open the door to Democratic-led congressional investigations targeting the president.
Several Supreme Court rulings last year and this year have helped Republicans, on balance, make the national House map more favorable to their party in the election, though polls indicate Democrats still are in a strong position to secure a majority.
The court has a 6-3 conservative majority. In a pair of landmark rulings powered by the conservative justices, the court in April gutted a key provision of [USN:S0N3YR00L TEXT:"the Voting Rights Act"], the 1965 law intended to prevent racial discrimination in voting, and in June threw out longstanding [USN:L1N4310Y4 TEXT:"campaign finance limits"] — decisions that have boosted Republicans.
But when the court issued a ruling last month rebuffing a Trump-backed effort to [USN:S0N431004 TEXT:"restrict mail voting"] — a mode of casting a ballot used more often by Democratic voters — only the court's two most conservative justices, Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, publicly dissented.
Republicans seem to have gained a net benefit from the court's recent election-related rulings, according to law professor Ilya Somin of George Mason University in Virginia, who said some of the key decisions "reflect longstanding conservative jurisprudential priorities."
Somin also noted the volume of litigation this cycle, saying, "It strikes me there are a lot more Supreme Court election-related cases than usual, especially in a midterm election."
REDISTRICTING ARMS RACE The court's decision that further undercut the Voting Rights Act made it harder for minorities to challenge electoral maps as racially discriminatory. Several Republican-led Southern states responded by rushing to dismantle House districts with sizable Black populations in time for the midterms. Black voters tend to support Democratic candidates.
Other Supreme Court rulings allowed starkly partisan voting maps for the midterms, fueling an unprecedented redistricting arms race between Republicans and Democrats. This battle was initiated last year when Trump urged Republican-led states to rip up existing congressional maps and draw new ones more likely to help the party pick up House seats in the midterms. Texas was the first to do so, and the Supreme Court [USN:S0N3VN017 TEXT:"allowed the new map"].
Redistricting traditionally has been carried out by state legislatures at the start of each new decade to reflect population shifts measured by the US Census, not midway through the decade as numerous states have done recently.
Kagan, one of the court's three liberal justices, lamented a 2019 [USN:L1N3Z50PN TEXT:"decision"] powered by the conservative justices that helped supercharge this political practice — called gerrymandering — that polling shows most Americans oppose. That ruling, authored by conservative Chief Justice John Roberts, declared that federal courts have [USN:KCN1TS2VP TEXT:"no authority"] to curb gerrymandering done for partisan gain.
Kagan [USN:L1N46700J TEXT:"accused"] the court's conservatives of having enabled increased political polarization by not reining in partisan gerrymandering, which involves states redrawing the boundaries of electoral districts based on the partisan leanings of voters to boost a political party's candidates.
"It is making what I think is unfortunately a too-polarized country even more so," Kagan told an audience at Catholic University's law school in Washington, expressing concern over implications for American democracy.
CAMPAIGN FINANCE The Supreme Court handed Republicans a set of wins on the issue of campaign finance this year. In June, it struck down federal caps on [USN:L1N4310Y4 TEXT:"spending by political parties"] in coordination with candidates in a challenge brought by Trump's vice president, JD Vance, and others. Since then, Republican committees have greatly exceeded these former limits, with their Democratic counterparts doing so to a lesser extent.
The court further bolstered coordinated spending this month by allowing a Trump administration policy giving political parties, and not just candidates, access to [USN:S0N45602X TEXT:"discounted TV and radio"] advertising rates.
The record for Trump and his political allies has not been perfect at the court, however. The justices last month [USN:S0N43100X TEXT:"barred Missouri"] from using its redrawn pro-Republican congressional map. And while the court permitted Texas to implement its pro-Republican congressional map, it subsequently allowed California's [USN:S0N3WN09U TEXT:"pro-Democratic map"].
Additionally, the court declined last month to let the US Postal Service enforce a rule [USN:S0N431004 TEXT:"targeting mail-in ballots"], following a June decision by the justices endorsing [USN:S0N40Z03J TEXT:"grace periods for mail voting"], over Republican objections.
All told, however, the court's election-related rulings so far this cycle have favored the election priorities of Trump and his party, reflecting a broader pattern, according to University of Illinois Chicago law professor Steve Schwinn.
"Court rulings this year and over the last decade have decidedly tilted the political playing field in favor of Republicans," Schwinn said.
MORE LITIGATION POSSIBLE Trump's history of challenging unfavorable electoral outcomes, including his false claims of widespread voting fraud in the 2020 election he lost to Democrat Joe Biden, suggests the court may be drawn into more electoral disputes after the midterms. State election officials across the country already are bracing for potential federal interference in the voting.
The Supreme Court turned away cases in which Trump and his allies challenged the 2020 election outcome. But it subsequently embraced his request for [USN:L1N3IQ192 TEXT:"criminal immunity"] after Trump was indicted on federal charges over his efforts to undo his loss to Biden.
"I think additional election litigation is quite likely," George Mason's Somin said. "Whether any of it reaches the Supreme Court is much harder to predict. The court, of course, has broad discretion over which cases it decides to take."
items.raw_description: The November 3 midterm elections are quickly approaching after an electoral cycle shaped to an unusual degree by decisions of the US Supreme Court, a development that prompted Justice Elena Kagan to voice alarm this week.

items.title: Investors see risk from US midterms to AI trade as data center backlash builds
items.author: Lewis Krauskopf
items.creator: Lewis Krauskopf
items.summary: Public opposition to data centers may jolt the AI trade as the US midterm elections approach, with a strong Democratic showing potentially hampering the buildout that has lifted stocks.
items.body:
Public opposition to data centers may jolt the AI trade as the US midterm elections approach, with a strong Democratic showing potentially hampering the buildout that has lifted stocks.
AI has driven the US stock bull market that just marked its [USN:L6N45R12W TEXT:"fourth anniversary"], as companies such as Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) pour money into building data centers. AI's importance to the market makes investors highly sensitive to obstacles that could slow the development pace, with spending on data centers and other AI infrastructure expected to top $1 trillion next year, [USN:L6N45K12P TEXT:"boosting corporate profits"].
Public backlash is one of those obstacles. As the massive data centers proliferate, many Americans are concerned about the strain on the environment and impact on energy costs, as well as about the technology itself.
"This is and has become a very tangible issue," said Christopher Gannatti, US chief investment officer at WisdomTree. Since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022, he said, "the key signal for the market has been how much money are these five or six huge companies spending" on data centers.
Investors have banked on an optimistic outlook for AI expansion, and any question about its rapid growth continuing causes sharp market moves. Several segments of the AI sector have stumbled in recent weeks as debt concerns centered on [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"cloud company CoreWeave"] (CRWV.O) .
Democratic victories in both chambers in the November 3 elections, which would wrest control of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republican Party, pose the greatest AI-related threats of the potential midterm outcomes, market watchers say. A Democratic sweep of the Senate and House of Representatives is the most likely outcome, according to trading on prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket.
Analysts are dubious about prospects for national legislation that would significantly stall data center construction. However, they say Democratic leadership of the House and Senate would likely mean more hearings and investigations related to AI and the data center buildout.
Investors are also focused on state and local races where data centers have become pivotal issues and where authorities also hold sway over the pace of development.
DEMOCRATIC CONGRESS COULD INCREASE AI SCRUTINY AI is not purely a partisan issue, as Republican voters also express concerns about data centers, but opposition appears stronger among Democrats. A Reuters/Ipsos poll released this month showed 69% of Democratic registered voters back limits on building data centers, compared with 43% of Republicans.
Even with a Democratic sweep, analysts doubt a bill that significantly impedes data center expansion would become law.
Trump — who has been supportive of AI — would likely block such legislation, said Matt Gertken, chief geopolitical strategist at BCA Research.
"The bill that is going to pass, and the bill that Trump is willing to sign, will be an AI regulation bill, but it probably won't be slamming the brakes on capex and construction," Gertken said.
[USN:FWN4661WE TEXT:"Trump said on Wednesday"] that companies building data centers should pay a "dividend" to communities if they want to make them popular.
Some in Congress, even on the Democratic side, might also be reluctant to enact legislation that undermines data center progress, due to its importance for economic growth and because of fears of losing competitive ground to China.
Still, if they control Congress, the Democrats are expected to apply more scrutiny to AI, including data centers, which could raise market volatility.
"There will be congressional hearings. There will be investigations," said Brian Gardner, chief Washington policy strategist at investment bank Stifel. "You never know where that stuff leads, and there can be negative headlines."
LOCAL RACES IN FOCUS FOR DATA CENTER OVERSIGHT The oversight that state and local authorities have over data centers also means investors will be unusually focused on specific elections next month. Investors are watching at least a half dozen states such as Texas for which party wins control of the governor's seat or the legislature, while also following specific House and Senate elections and even votes for positions such as utility commissioner.
"Data centers are a real political issue, a really salient one in these state and local races," said Maxwell Shulman, a policy research analyst at Beacon Policy Advisors in Washington. "And depending on which party takes control, there really could be implications for the regulations and the restrictions that data centers might have to face going forward."
Strategists at investment bank Morgan Stanley are monitoring the elections for governor in Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Georgia, Nevada, Wisconsin and Michigan.
"Because it is so disproportionate, the states where that investment is going really do have to be a focus for investors," Shulman said.
Policy uncertainty around data centers is unlikely to "derail" the AI investment theme, said Kevin Shea, senior equity analyst at BNY Wealth. "But what it can do is disrupt the timing and the cost," Shea said.

items.title: Saudi Aramco tells staff to evacuate Dhahran headquarters, sources say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Oil giant Saudi Aramco has instructed staff to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran and work remotely, six people with knowledge of the matter said on Thursday.
items.body:
Oil giant Saudi Aramco (2223.SE) has instructed staff to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran and work remotely, six people with knowledge of the matter said on Thursday.
Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The move marked the first time Aramco had asked staff to evacuate its headquarters since the start of the Iran war .
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis caused [USN:L1N46710X TEXT:"extensive damage"] to the company's headquarters earlier this month when they struck the building, with fire spreading across several floors.
The facility hosts an operations centre, which helps the world's largest oil company oversee onshore and offshore oil rigs, refineries, export terminals and thousands of kilometres of pipelines.
Separately, two people were killed on Wednesday after Saudi air defences intercepted a drone that was attempting to hit a facility at Aramco's Shaybah oilfield.
Saudi Arabia has responded to Houthi attacks with a wave of strikes on missile launcher sites, vowing to protect the kingdom, and says it has intercepted many ballistic missiles fired by the group.

By Olena Harmash and Gleb Bryanski
KYIV/MOSCOW, Oct 22 (Reuters) – Russia pounded Kyiv with ballistic missiles and Ukraine sent hundreds of drones towards Moscow overnight as the warring sides kept up a barrage of attacks despite the latest US push to end the conflict.

Russia said on Wednesday it was ready to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month, after President Vladimir Putin hosted US envoy Steve Witkoff for talks in St Petersburg.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he hoped negotiations, which would be the first since February, would take place early in November.

Show Full Article

Ukraine said Russia fired at least 21 ballistic missiles in three waves. Russia said Ukraine launched 630 drones towards the capital Moscow during the night.

The two sides held an exchange of war dead, with Moscow handing over 252 bodies and Ukraine handing over 25, according to the Belta state news agency in neighbouring Belarus. Such exchanges have accompanied moves towards talks in the past.

But while Witkoff spoke of “some degree of momentum” after meeting Zelenskiy and European and NATO officials in Oslo earlier in the week, the Kremlin expressed doubts.

“The Americans sensed some new nuances (in Oslo) and told us about this. But these nuances, so to speak, do not entirely satisfy us,” Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said.

A senior Russian official, briefed on the results of the Putin-Witkoff talks, said they were relatively short and not substantive. The American brought a set of proposals drafted in Oslo and handed them to Putin for review, the person said.

Another source close to the Kremlin said the US proposals included a scenario where Ukraine would cede all of its Donbas region to Russia in return for receiving a guarantee of its future security from NATO.

Russia says it launched the war, the deadliest in Europe since World War Two, in part to prevent Ukraine from joining NATO. It has repeatedly said it would not end fighting unless Ukraine cedes more land, limits the size of its forces and is permanently barred from forming alliances.

Ukraine, which says the invasion was an unprovoked war of conquest, has long dismissed Russia’s conditions as a demand for capitulation that would leave it defenceless against future Russian attacks.

US PRAISE FOR ‘HUMANITARIAN’ PUTIN GOES DOWN BADLY WITH KYIV

Zelenskiy’s meeting with Witkoff was aimed in part at smoothing over a deterioration in relations with Washington this month, after President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel and lifted sanctions on Moscow.

Kyiv says Washington failed to provide early-warning data on Russian missile launches, throttled the SpaceX satellite system used to guide Ukrainian drones, and withheld missile defence systems bought on its behalf by Europeans. Washington denies any shift in policy to intentionally hamper Ukraine’s forces.

Trump has repeatedly rebuked Ukraine for attacking Russian oil refineries while saying little about far deadlier Russian attacks on Ukraine. He called for Zelenskiy to be replaced and said Russia’s actions in Ukraine have been “fine”.

Zelenskiy, who long avoided any criticism of the Trump administration, has increasingly pushed back against what he describes as a shift towards sympathy with Moscow.

On Thursday Zelenskiy snapped back at Witkoff for saluting Putin as a “humanitarian” during his visit to Russia, when the US envoy thanked Putin for releasing a 74-year-old American captured by Russian forces in Ukraine.

“Three waves of ballistic missiles have been launched at Kyiv by Russian ‘humanitarians’ since yesterday evening,” Zelenskiy posted on X. “They used 21 missiles. Unfortunately, numerous sites across the city have been hit and damaged.”

He said 2 people were killed and 34 injured, including five children, in attacks on a dozen Ukrainian regions.

Russia said it carried out a “massive strike” overnight on port infrastructure in Ukraine’s Odesa region, as well as on vessels used by the Ukrainian military.

In Russia, two people were wounded near Moscow by drones launched towards the capital during the night, Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on Telegram. Most of the drones were downed at long range, he added.

In the Russian border region of Belgorod, one man was killed and another wounded by Ukrainian drones, local officials said.

With the frontlines of the war largely static, both sides have escalated long-range air strikes this year. Russia has particularly targeted the Ukrainian power grid, while Ukraine has aimed at Russian oil refineries. Both have struck data centres, commercial warehouses and Black Sea shipping.

The war has ground on for more than 4-1/2 years, defying Trump’s pledge during his 2024 election campaign that he could end it in a day. No breakthrough emerged from three short meetings in Istanbul last year and three rounds of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi and Geneva at the start of this year.

(Reporting by Olena Harmash and Gleb Garanich in Kyiv, Gleb Bryanski in Moscow, Darya Korsunskaya in London and Jekaterīna Golubkova in TokyoWriting by Mark Trevelyan and Peter Graff)

items.title: World shares retreat as report of damage to oil tankers pushes oil prices higher
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: World shares and U.S. futures retreated on Thursday as oil prices jumped more than 2 per cent following a report by Iran’s state television that seven oil tankers caught fire and were damaged in the ...
items.body: World shares and U.S. futures retreated on Thursday as oil prices jumped more than 2 per cent following a report by Iran’s state television that seven oil tankers caught fire and were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz. If the report is verified, it would be the largest number of vessels damaged in the waterway in a single day since the start of the Iran war on Feb. 28. Brent crude, the international standard, gained 3.2 per cent to US$112.27 per barrel. It has been bouncing between $97 and $112 in recent days on uncertainty about when the war with Iran will allow the global energy industry to return to normal. U.S. benchmark crude rose 2.8 per cent to $99.80 per barrel. In early European trading, Germany’s DAX shed 1.1 per cent to 25,367.96, while the CAC 40 in Paris declined 1.3 per cent to 7,816.67. Britain’s FTSE 100 was down 0.7 per cent at 10,678.67. The future for the S&P 500 lost 1 per cent and that for the Dow Jones Industrial Average was 0.7 per cent lower. In Asia, Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 lost 2.7 per cent to 62,907.84 on heavy selling of big tech companies like SoftBank Group, which lost 6.9 per cent. Computer chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron fell 7 per cent and testing equipment maker Advantest lost 6 per cent. In South Korea, the Kospi dropped 3.5 per cent, to 5,533.77. Big memory chipmakers led the decline, with Samsung Electronics down 4 per cent. SK Hynix lost 5.5 per cent. AI stocks, at the center of market action in recent months, are under pressure from worries that construction of data centers may slow as it is becoming increasingly expensive to borrow money. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng shed 3 per cent to 22,934.68, and the Shanghai Composite index gave up 1.5 per cent to 3,658.03. Taiwan’s Taiex lost 1.8 per cent. In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 declined 0.4 per cent to 8,793.20. The U.S. stock market rose Wednesday following strong profit reports from SpaceX, Capital One Financial and other big companies. The S&P 500 added 0.6 per cent and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.7 per cent. The Nasdaq composite climbed 1.1 per cent. SpaceX helped lead the market and climbed 7.8 per cent after reporting a stronger profit for the summer than analysts expected. Elon Musk, who runs the company that makes money from artificial-intelligence technology, rockets and other businesses, also said that SpaceX took a step to consider a possible merger with Tesla, his electric-vehicle company. Tesla rose 3.4 per cent and was one of the strongest forces lifting the S&P 500. Other stocks rallying on profit reports that topped analysts’ expectations included Capital One Financial, which rose 2.5 per cent, and Winnebago Industries, which climbed 10.7 per cent. Expectations are high for profit growth for all kinds of companies during the summer, and they need to meet them to justify the big runs their stock prices have made despite worries about high inflation, higher interest rates and other challenges weighing on Wall Street. Netflix fell 5.3 per cent even though the streaming service reported a stronger profit than analysts expected. Investors focused instead on worries that Netflix’s momentum may be slowing. In other dealings early Thursday, the U.S. dollar fell to 157.22 Japanese yen from 158.14 yen late Wednesday. The euro slipped to US$1.1231 from $1.1233. Elaine Kurtenbach, The Associated Press

items.title: India's Jindal Stainless beats quarterly profit view on strong exports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: India's Jindal Stainless reported an 11.1% rise in second-quarter profit on Thursday, led by strong sales volume growth, especially in exports.
items.body:
India's Jindal Stainless (JIST.NS) reported an 11.1% rise in second-quarter profit on Thursday, led by strong sales volume growth, especially in exports.
Here are some key details:
Consolidated net profit for India's biggest stainless-steel producer rose to 8.98 billion rupees ($94.7 million) in the quarter ended September 30 from 8.08 billion rupees a year ago
Analysts, on average, had expected a profit of 8.36 billion rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG
Higher volumes and resilient stainless steel demand were expected to boost second-quarter earnings, according to analysts at ICICI Securities
Sales volume rose 2.5% year-on-year to 664,378 tons, led by a 36% jump in exports
Domestic sales comprised 89% of total sales, down from 91% a year ago, while exports were 11% of total sales during the quarter
Revenue rose 18.2% to 128.74 billion rupees; EBITDA grew 3.2% year-on-year to 14.33 billion rupees
The quarter marked a resilient recovery following the operational disruptions in the previous three months, which had been impacted by the geopolitical situation and industrial gas availability constraints - Jindal Stainless
The company also flagged increased import pressure, especially from China
"The first four months of FY27 alone account for about 63% of the entire previous year's imports from China," the stainless steel maker said
Jindal Stainless operates 16 stainless-steel facilities across India, Spain and Indonesia, with a network spanning 12 countries
($1 = 94.8800 Indian rupees)

items.title: 中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝ＡＩ関連主導で下落、ＣＳＩ３００弱気相場入り
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [上海／香港 ２２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[上海／香港 ２２日 ロイター] - 中国・香港株式市場は下落。中国の主要株価指数ＣＳＩ３００指数は１５カ月ぶりの安値となり弱気相場入りが確認された。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株が、成長とバリュエーションの持続性に対する懸念から急落したことが背景。

ＣＳＩ３００指数は１．８％下落し、４０３６．３０で終了。２０２５年７月以来の安値となった。６月２２日に付けた終値ベースの直近高値から２０．２％下落し、弱気相場の目安とされる２０％下落の水準を超えた。

終値ベースでは、同指数は２００７年に付けた高値を更新しておらず、６月に相場を５年ぶりの高値に押し上げた勢いはその後急速に反転した。

香港のロータス・アセット・マネジメントのマネジングパートナー兼最高投資責任者（ＣＩＯ）、ハオ・ホン氏は「市場は底なしの状況だ」と述べた。

上海総合指数は１．５％下落して終了し１年超ぶりの安値となった。

アジア全域のハイテク主力株に広がった売り、低調な景気刺激策への期待、新たな材料の欠如を背景に、中国市場で広範な売りが加速した。

上昇したのは生活必需品指数と公益事業指数のみ。

ホン氏は「国家隊はためらっている」とし、売り局面でしばしば介入する中国の国有投資ファンドに言及した。

ＣＳＩ半導体指数は３．６％下落、ＣＳＩ人工知能指数は３．３％下落した。深セン証券取引所の新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は４．４％急落し、２５年７月以来の安値を付けた。

トレーダーやアナリストによると、中国政府の小出しの景気刺激策への失望も市場心理の重しとなっている。また、第３・四半期の経済成長率が予想を上回ったことで、追加の政策支援への期待が後退した。

＜課税問題が重しとなる香港市場＞

香港市場では、ハンセン指数が３％下落し、４カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。ハンセンテック指数は５％下落し、２年ぶりの安値となった。

一部の投資家は、香港上場の中国企業の株主の多くが採用している一般的な仕組みであるオフショア信託に対し、中国政府が所得税の徴収を進める取り組みを、売り圧力のもう一つの要因として指摘した。

ロータスのホン氏は、きょうが税申告の最終日だと指摘。過去数週間の売りは、中国企業の創業者らが主導したとし「納税義務を果たすための現金を調達するため、資産を売却していたのは明らかだ」と述べた。

２２日の下落が大きかった銘柄では、テンセントが２．９％下落、アリババが６％超急落した。

盛期資本（香港）のゼン・ウェンカイＣＩＯは「これほど急激かつ急速な下落は非常にまれで、特にテンセントのような主力銘柄ではなおさらだ。これはおそらくパニック売りの最終局面で、市場の売りは終わりに近づいている」と説明。「ただ、これほどの傷からの回復には時間がかかるだろう」と語った。

香港市場では、ハンセン指数が３％下落し、４カ月ぶりの安値を付けた。ハンセンテック指数は５％下落し、２年ぶりの安値となった。

一部の投資家は、香港上場の中国企業の株主の多くが採用している一般的な仕組みであるオフショア信託に対し、中国政府が所得税の徴収を進める取り組みを、売り圧力のもう一つの要因として指摘した。

ロータスのホン氏は、きょうが税申告の最終日だと指摘。過去数週間の売りは、中国企業の創業者らが主導したとし「納税義務を果たすための現金を調達するため、資産を売却していたのは明らかだ」と述べた。

２２日の下落が大きかった銘柄では、テンセントが２．９％下落、アリババが６％超急落した。

盛期資本（香港）のゼン・ウェンカイＣＩＯは「これほど急激かつ急速な下落は非常にまれで、特にテンセントのような主力銘柄ではなおさらだ。これはおそらくパニック売りの最終局面で、市場の売りは終わりに近づいている」と説明。「ただ、これほどの傷からの回復には時間がかかるだろう」と語った。

items.title: Lab testing LBO offers murky result for both sides
items.author: Aimee Donnellan
items.creator: Aimee Donnellan
items.summary: EQT will buy Qiagen for $12 bln, whose kits trace diseases and help police solve crimes. It’s barely more than an offer shareholders rejected back in 2020. Yet the Swedish buyer will need to grow beyond current forecasts and crank up margins to get a decent return.
items.body:
EQT will buy Qiagen for $12 bln, whose kits trace diseases and help police solve crimes. It’s barely more than an offer shareholders rejected back in 2020. Yet the Swedish buyer will need to grow beyond current forecasts and crank up margins to get a decent return.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Aimee Donnellan on LinkedIn .
CONTEXT NEWS Sweden's EQT will buy molecular testing company Qiagen for about €9.6 billion ($10.78 billion), the companies said on October 21.
Buyout firm EQT offered €46.50 ($52.22) a share for Qiagen, representing an 8.6% premium to its last close. Affiliates of the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board are also participating in the offer.
The deal, which values Qiagen at about $12.1 billion including about $1.1 billion in net debt, is expected to close in mid-2027. EQT has secured equity and debt financing to fund the offer.
Qiagen said it was suspending its full-year 2026 outlook pending the deal. It reported preliminary third-quarter net sales of $548 million and adjusted diluted earnings per share of $0.65.
Qiagen shares were trading at €45.12 ($50.70) by 0833 GMT on October 22.

items.title: Southern Italy truckers ease protests as government lines up aid
items.author: Francesca Piscioneri, Alvise Armellini
items.creator: Francesca Piscioneri, Alvise Armellini
items.summary: Truck drivers' protests that have seriously affected fuel and food supplies in southern Italy were easing on Thursday as Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government was lining up aid and taking a harder line against roadblocks.
items.body:
Truck drivers' protests that have seriously affected [USN:L8N467269 TEXT:"fuel and food supplies"] in southern Italy were easing on Thursday as Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government was lining up aid and taking a harder line against roadblocks.
Since last week, hauliers have been blocking roads and motorways to protest against high fuel prices, but their representatives said roadblocks would be lifted in Sicily following talks with the government.
Truck drivers in Calabria also suspended their protest, while Vincenzo Parisi, speaking for hauliers from the Campania region around Naples, told RAI public radio he hoped roadblocks could be lifted in the area later on Thursday.
SEVERE DISRUPTION, BUT NO TOILET PAPER SHORTAGES The protests have caused "severe disruption" in Campania, affecting supplies to supermarkets, petrol stations and even hospitals, Deputy Infrastructure Minister Edoardo Rixi told RAI radio.
However, Meloni's office dismissed as "ridiculous" a front-page report by opposition newspaper Il Fatto Quotidiano suggesting that government headquarters in Rome were running out of toilet paper due to the truckers' blockades.
In Naples, fuel shortages were making it harder for doctors to reach hospitals and clinics and for ambulances to respond to emergencies, the head of the local order of physicians and dentists said.
"We understand the truck drivers' concerns, but we are calling for a responsible protest. Fuel supplies for ambulances must be guaranteed and healthcare workers must be able to get to work," Bruno Zuccarelli said.
MELONI TO CHAIR MEETING ON APPROVING AID Antonio Ferraioli, chairman and chief executive of tomato sauce and pasta producer La Doria, told la Repubblica daily that the company had stopped production in seven plants in southern Italy and placed half of its workforce on forced leave.
"If the protest continues, products from southern Italy will disappear from supermarket shelves across the country and will be replaced by imports or products from other parts of Italy," he said.
Meloni was due to chair a cabinet meeting in Rome to approve a decree bringing together aid measures for truck drivers and farmers, including financial compensation measures for high diesel costs.
The government also said it was working to ensure the distribution of essential goods, including food and medicines, offering police escorts to trucks seeking to go past roadblocks.
items.raw_description: Truck drivers' protests that have seriously affected fuel and food supplies in southern Italy were easing on Thursday as Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government was lining up aid and taking a harder line against roadblocks.

items.title: Índice das principais empresas da China confirma mercado em baixa; setor de IA tem forte queda
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O índice das principais ações da China despencou para a menor cotação em 15 meses e confirmou um mercado em baixa nesta quinta-feira, à medida que as ações do setor de IA caíram devido a temores de que o crescimento e as valorizações fossem insustentáveis.
items.body:
O índice das principais ações da China despencou para a menor cotação em 15 meses e confirmou um mercado em baixa nesta quinta-feira, à medida que as ações do setor de IA caíram devido a temores de que o crescimento e as valorizações fossem insustentáveis.
O Índice CSI300 (.CSI300) caiu 1,8%, fechando em 4.036,30, seu nível mais baixo desde julho de 2025. Ele está agora 20,2% abaixo de sua última alta de fechamento, registrada em 22 de junho, ultrapassando o limiar de 20% que normalmente define um mercado em baixa.
O Índice Composto de Xangai (.SSEC) fechou com queda de 1,5%, também seu nível mais baixo em mais de um ano.
Com base nos níveis de fechamento, o índice CSI300 nunca superou a alta registrada em 2007, e o ímpeto que levou o mercado a uma alta de cinco anos em junho sofreu uma reversão acentuada desde então.
"O mercado está em baixa", disse Hao Hong, sócio-gerente e diretor de investimentos da Lotus Asset Management, em Hong Kong.
Uma onda generalizada de vendas entre as principais empresas de tecnologia em toda a Ásia, aliada a expectativas moderadas de estímulos e à falta de novos catalisadores, desencadeou uma forte queda na China.
Apenas os subíndices de bens de consumo básico (.CSI000912) e de serviços públicos (.CSI000917) conseguiram registrar ganhos modestos.
O Índice CSI de chips (.CSI931865) caiu 3,6% e o Índice CSI de IA (.CSI930713) registrou queda de 3,3%. O Índice Composto ChiNext (.CNT) , da bolsa para startups, despencou 4,4%, atingindo seu nível mais baixo desde julho de 2025.
O humor do mercado também foi prejudicado pela decepção com as medidas de estímulo fragmentadas de Pequim, segundo operadores e analistas, enquanto o crescimento econômico no terceiro trimestre, acima do esperado, reduziu ainda mais as expectativas de apoio adicional por parte das autoridades.
O crescimento econômico da China saiu de níveis mínimos de três anos, já que as exportações compensaram a cautela dos consumidores em gastar, mesmo com a crescente dependência de fatores externos aprofundando os desequilíbrios estruturais.
. Em TÓQUIO, o índice Nikkei (.N225) caiu 2,67%, a 62.907,84 pontos.
. Em HONG KONG, o índice HANG SENG (.HSI) caiu 3,03%, a 22.934 pontos.
. Em XANGAI, o índice SSEC (.SSEC) perdeu 1,48%, a 3.658 pontos.
. O índice CSI300 (.CSI300) , que reúne as maiores companhias listadas em XANGAI e SHENZHEN, retrocedeu 1,84%, a 4.036 pontos.
. Em SEUL, o índice KOSPI (.KS11) teve desvalorização de 3,52%, a 5.533 pontos.
. Em TAIWAN, o índice TAIEX (.TWII) registrou baixa de 1,81%, a 46.041 pontos.
. Em CINGAPURA, o índice STRAITS TIMES (.STI) desvalorizou-se 0,57%, a 5.406 pontos.
. Em SYDNEY o índice S&P/ASX 200 (.AXJO) recuou 0,43%, a 8.793 pontos.
(Reportagem da Redação de Xangai e de Hong Kong)

items.title: Pound edges higher, outperforming as investor nerves rattle euro zone markets
items.author: Amanda Cooper
items.creator: Amanda Cooper
items.summary: The pound edged up on Thursday, as outflows from euro zone assets saw UK stocks, bonds and the currency outperform other markets in the region.
items.body:
The pound edged up on Thursday, as outflows from euro zone assets saw UK stocks, bonds and the currency outperform other markets in the region.
Expectations that the Bank of England will raise interest rates next month are also supporting the pound, following higher than expected UK inflation [USN:L8N46708O TEXT:"data"] this week.
Sterling was up 0.1% on the day at $1.34, making it one of the stronger performers, aside from the safe-haven Japanese yen and Swiss franc .
Money markets show traders expect the Bank of England to deliver at least three quarter-point rate hikes by April, with the first one priced in for the November 5 policy meeting, compared with roughly two hikes by the European Central Bank, thereby widening the interest-rate differential that fuels carry trades.
These are lucrative rate-plays that involve borrowing a lower-yielding currency, in this case, the euro, to sell it and fund investment in a higher-yielding currency like the pound.
Investor concern about high oil prices, the cost of the AI buildout and the ability of developed-market governments to bring down their huge debt loads rattled riskier assets, particularly in Europe, where French bond yields rose to new 24-year highs and euro zone stocks fell sharply.
UK gilt yields were flat on the day , against steep rises in yields on French, Italian and Belgian debt, while the FTSE 100 (.FTSE) fell 0.6% but outperformed the STOXX 600 (.STOXX) , which was down 1%.
Over the course of the last month, the pound has been the best-performing major currency against the US dollar, up 0.3%, while the euro is the worst-performing, with a loss of 2%.
The euro is heading for a fourth straight week of declines against the pound , having lost another 0.5% so far this week, which brings its decline for the year to 1.8%. If sustained, this would be the euro's largest monthly drop against the pound since May 2023, when it fell 2%.
"It looks like there is both independent sterling strength and independent euro weakness at play in euro/sterling. Earlier this summer, we had felt that sterling gains would not last. But now greater market confidence in a Bank of England tightening cycle – we look for 25-bp hikes in February and November – makes sterling a high-carry European currency," ING strategist Chris Turner said.
The concern building over the ability of the French government to tackle its finances is also taking its toll on the euro, which traders are betting will fall further against the pound. The options market shows traders are at their most negative over the prospects of the euro against the pound since mid-2024 , according to LSEG data.
UK finance minister John Healey delivers his first budget on [USN:L8N46716U TEXT:"October 28"], which major investors expect to pass without rattling markets unduly.

items.title: Manchester City take perfect record to Villa amid off-field turmoil
items.author: Lori Ewing
items.creator: Lori Ewing
items.summary: Manchester City will try to preserve the Premier League's only perfect record at Aston Villa this weekend while dealing with mounting injuries and major off-field distractions following their guilty verdict on financial-rule charges.
items.body:
Manchester City will try to preserve the Premier League's only perfect record at Aston Villa this weekend while dealing with mounting injuries and major off-field distractions following their [USN:L6N45L10G TEXT:"guilty verdict"] on financial-rule charges.
Enzo Maresca's City have won all seven league matches to sit three points clear of champions Arsenal, but an independent commission's finding that the club were guilty of 114 financial breaches has cast a shadow over their blistering start.
City have denied any wrongdoing and appealed, with sanctions yet to be decided.
Their immediate task is maintaining their flawless run at Villa Park on Saturday despite a growing injury list.
Forward [USN:L6N4650QO TEXT:"Antoine Semenyo"] is set for a lengthy spell out with a knee injury, while wing back Nico O'Reilly and midfielders Mateo Kovacic and Matheus Nunes are doubts.
League-leading scorer Erling Haaland was rested for Tuesday's [USN:L6N4661C4 TEXT:"5-1"] Champions League thrashing of AEK Athens because of a knock but is expected to be available against Villa.
Arsenal, City's closest challengers on 18 points, host Everton on Saturday, although they have fitness concerns after [USN:L1N46802Z TEXT:"Bukayo Saka"] limped off in the 10th minute of Wednesday's [USN:L6N46717X TEXT:"2-2"] Champions League draw at Bayern Munich with a quadriceps injury.
"He doesn't look good at all, but we'll have to wait and see," Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said.
Fourth-placed Chelsea host London rivals Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Saturday after back-to-back league victories over Bournemouth and Everton.
Spurs finally earned their first league victory of the season with Monday's [USN:L6N4651AC TEXT:"3-1"] home win over Coventry City after a miserable start that has left them 16th with six points from seven games. Chelsea have 13 points.
Liverpool face one of the tougher challenges of the weekend when they welcome high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion to Anfield on Sunday.
Brighton's superb start has them third with five wins and a draw from seven matches, two places and four points above Liverpool, while their goal difference of plus 18 is the league's best.
Liverpool, though, have uncovered another attacking weapon in 18-year-old [USN:L8N4662MN TEXT:"Rio Ngumoha"], who produced a dazzling performance in their 4-3 Champions League comeback win over Villarreal on Tuesday.
Ngumoha created two goals and became the youngest Liverpool player to register a Champions League assist, earning a standing ovation from the Anfield crowd.
"That's the good thing with Rio he is still 18, he is not the full package, he can add things fortunately for us. Hopefully he can continue in the same way," Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said. "But I'm happy because attitude-wise I think he's in a great place."
Liverpool's injury problems complicate the task, with the versatile Dominik Szoboszlai, wing back Jeremie Frimpong, right back Conor Bradley and striker Hugo Ekitike among those sidelined.
At Old Trafford, Manchester United desperately need a victory over Bournemouth to breathe life into a season that has gone awry.
Michael Carrick's team are 13th with one victory and seven points from their opening seven matches and are coming off a shambolic [USN:L6N4671CM TEXT:"4-1"] Champions League defeat at Como on Wednesday.
"I have to apologise to the supporters," Carrick said after the latest setback in Italy. "I care about this football club as much as anyone, if not more.
"For us to play in that way, it's not acceptable. That bit of intensity, that aggression, that real willingness to give everything tonight was totally the opposite of the performance. It was tough to watch."
Complicating matters, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Lisandro Martinez are among those with injury or fitness concerns, while midfielder Manuel Ugarte has a long-term knee injury.
Carrick's United were held 1-1 at home by Tottenham and away to Leeds United in their last two league outings and now face a Bournemouth side who sit one point below them.
For Manchester City, the challenge is almost the reverse. While their rivals search for momentum or try to keep pace, they head to Villa attempting to ensure the legal fight surrounding the club does not interrupt a perfect start on the pitch.
items.raw_description: Manchester City will try to preserve the Premier League's only perfect record at Aston Villa this weekend while dealing with mounting injuries and major off-field distractions following their guilty verdict on financial-rule charges.

items.title: Turkey says it is waiting for sale contract from Qatar for Eurofighter Typhoon jet procurement
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Turkey is waiting for Qatar to send it a sale contract and a draft training programme as part of its deal with Britain to procure Eurofighter Typhoon jets, the Turkish Defence Ministry said on Thursday.
items.body:
Turkey is waiting for Qatar to send it a sale contract and a draft training programme as part of its deal with Britain to procure Eurofighter Typhoon jets, the Turkish Defence Ministry said on Thursday.
NATO allies Turkey and Britain [USN:L1N3W80J0 TEXT:"signed the deal"] for 20 jets last year, in a move aimed at deepening bilateral ties and bolstering Turkish air defences. Ankara has said it was also seeking 24 more jets from Qatar and Oman, though there has been little progress on that procurement.
Under the deal with Britain, Qatar and Oman can supply Turkey with some of its own Typhoons, though that requires a separate sales contract.
At its weekly press briefing, the ministry said that [USN:L8N3WB0U6 TEXT:"talks on the procurement"] were continuing and that Turkish and Qatari delegations discussed technical and logistical matters in August and September. These included the scope of jets and ammunition to be procured, training for pilots and maintenance teams.
"It is expected for Qatar to prepare the draft training programme and the sales contract to be sent to our country," it said.
Turkey signed [USN:L6N4670S7 TEXT:"an accord"] with Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia on Wednesday to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities, including through joint development and production.
The ministry added that its defence budget was [USN:L8N4671F9 TEXT:"increased for 2027"] due to ongoing domestic defence industry projects for air defences and platforms, Turkey's indigenous KAAN fighter jet programme, drone development and shipbuilding.

Brighton's superb start has them third with five wins and a draw from seven matches, two places and four points above Liverpool, while their goal difference of plus 18 is the league's best.
Liverpool, though, have uncovered another attacking weapon in 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha, who produced a dazzling performance in their 4-3 Champions League comeback win over Villarreal on Tuesday.
Ngumoha created two goals and became the youngest Liverpool player to register a Champions League assist, earning a standing ovation from the Anfield crowd.
"That's the good thing with Rio he is still 18, he is not the full package, he can add things fortunately for us. Hopefully he can continue in the same way," Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said. "But I'm happy because attitude-wise I think he's in a great place."
Liverpool's injury problems complicate the task, with the versatile Dominik Szoboszlai, wing back Jeremie Frimpong, right back Conor Bradley and striker Hugo Ekitike among those sidelined.
At Old Trafford, Manchester United desperately need a victory over Bournemouth to breathe life into a season that has gone awry.
Michael Carrick's team are 13th with one victory and seven points from their opening seven matches and are coming off a shambolic 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como on Wednesday.
"I have to apologise to the supporters," Carrick said after the latest setback in Italy. "I care about this football club as much as anyone, if not more.
"For us to play in that way, it's not acceptable. That bit of intensity, that aggression, that real willingness to give everything tonight was totally the opposite of the performance. It was tough to watch."
Complicating matters, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Lisandro Martinez are among those with injury or fitness concerns, while midfielder Manuel Ugarte has a long-term knee injury.
Carrick's United were held 1-1 at home by Tottenham and away to Leeds United in their last two league outings and now face a Bournemouth side who sit one point below them.
For Manchester City, the challenge is almost the reverse. While their rivals search for momentum or try to keep pace, they head to Villa attempting to ensure the legal fight surrounding the club does not interrupt a perfect start on the pitch.

items.title: La prima de riesgo francesa marca un nuevo máximo de 15 años ante inquietudes fiscales y protestas
items.author: Stefano Rebaudo
items.creator: Stefano Rebaudo
items.summary: El diferencial de rendimiento entre los bonos del Estado francés a 10 años y los bonos alemanes, considerados activos refugio, alcanzaba el jueves un nuevo máximo de 15 años, mientras las dudas sobre la capacidad del país para sanear sus deterioradas finanzas públicas y las continuas protestas callejeras seguían lastrando la confianza de los inversores.
items.body:
El diferencial de rendimiento entre los bonos del Estado francés a 10 años y los bonos alemanes, considerados activos refugio, alcanzaba el jueves un nuevo máximo de 15 años, mientras las dudas sobre la capacidad del país para sanear sus deterioradas finanzas públicas y las continuas protestas callejeras seguían lastrando la confianza de los inversores.
Los ministros franceses han prometido reforzar considerablemente el dispositivo de seguridad durante las nuevas protestas previstas para este sábado, con un despliegue de militares junto con efectivos policiales adicionales.
El rendimiento del bono francés de referencia a 10 años subía 6 puntos básicos, hasta el 5,0601%, su nivel más alto desde julio de 2002.
Esto elevaba la prima de riesgo francesa frente a los bonos alemanes hasta los 160,90 puntos básicos —su mayor nivel desde noviembre de 2011, durante la crisis de deuda de la zona euro—, lo que reflejaba la inquietud de los inversores por las actuales perspectivas fiscales de Francia.
Los diferenciales de rendimiento frente a los bonos alemanes se ampliaban en toda la zona euro. El de Bélgica alcanzaba los 104,89 puntos básicos, su máximo desde 2013, mientras que el de Italia subía 4,5 puntos básicos, hasta los 116,90; el de España se ampliaba 3 puntos básicos, hasta los 66,50; y el de Grecia aumentaba 5,5 puntos básicos, hasta los 99,50.
La incertidumbre política ante las elecciones del próximo año en Francia y las dificultades de París para aprobar un presupuesto han lastrado aún más la confianza del mercado.
"Existe un consenso en que Europa está hoy mejor preparada para afrontar las crisis y en que las instituciones europeas son más fuertes que hace 15 años, lo que debería facilitar la articulación de una respuesta europea", dijo Giada Giani, economista de Citi, al referirse a las diferencias entre la Francia actual y los países de la periferia europea a principios de la década de 2010.
"Pero el resurgimiento del euroescepticismo supone una limitación en este caso", añadió.
El rendimiento de los bonos del Estado alemán a 10 años , referencia de la zona euro, bajaba 1,5 puntos básicos, hasta el 3,40%, mientras la demanda de bonos refugio sostenía sus precios. El rendimiento se ha movido entre aproximadamente el 3,40% y el 3,50% desde principios de este mes.
El rendimiento del bono alemán a dos años , más sensible a las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés oficiales, subía un punto básico, hasta el 3,05%.

items.title: Roche supera estimativas de receita, mas ações caem à medida que genéricos corroem vendas do Xolair
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A farmacêutica suíça Roche superou as expectativas de vendas do terceiro trimestre nesta quinta-feira, impulsionada pela demanda constante por medicamentos-chave, como o Ocrevus, para ganhar tempo enquanto busca no exterior reabastecer seu pipeline diante de expirações iminentes de patentes.
items.body:
A farmacêutica suíça Roche (ROPC.S) superou as expectativas de vendas do terceiro trimestre nesta quinta-feira, impulsionada pela demanda constante por medicamentos-chave, como o Ocrevus, para ganhar tempo enquanto busca no exterior reabastecer seu pipeline diante de expirações iminentes de patentes.
A receita do grupo cresceu 7% a taxas de câmbio constantes, atingindo 16,13 bilhões de francos suíços (US$19,61 bilhões), superando a previsão consensual elaborada pela empresa, de 15,75 bilhões de francos (US$19,15 bilhões).
No entanto, o trimestre trouxe um sinal precoce de pressão competitiva — as vendas do medicamento Xolair ficaram abaixo das previsões do mercado após o lançamento do primeiro genérico mais barato, gerando vendas de 848 milhões de francos (US$1,03 bilhão) contra expectativas de 925 milhões de francos (US$1,12 bilhão).
As ações caíam 1,1% no pregão da manhã.
Com vários medicamentos de grande sucesso mais antigos se aproximando do vencimento das patentes, a Roche aposta em seus principais produtos para impulsionar o crescimento no curto prazo, ao mesmo tempo em que intensifica as negociações externas para tratamentos de última geração. A empresa fechou um acordo no valor de mais de US$15 bilhões com a chinesa Hansoh Pharma, segundo notícia divulgada na segunda-feira.
Com foco no ecossistema de biotecnologia da Europa, o presidente-executivo Thomas Schinecker afirmou na quinta-feira que cerca de 50% dos acordos de licenciamento externos do grupo nos últimos quatro anos foram firmados nos EUA e os outros 50% na China e na Ásia.
“Isso mostra um pouco a situação em que a Europa se encontra em termos de inovação”, disse Schinecker.
A administração também observou que o impacto negativo das reformas nos preços dos serviços de saúde na China estava diminuindo, apesar das quedas de dois dígitos no país, com a divisão de diagnósticos — que cresceu 5%, para 3,54 bilhões de francos — devendo retornar a um crescimento “normal” na faixa de um dígito médio a alto no próximo ano.
A Roche também se beneficiou da estabilização do dólar em relação ao franco suíço, aliviando o impacto prolongado das taxas de câmbio no mercado norte-americano, que responde por quase metade da receita do grupo.
Os medicamentos mais vendidos impulsionaram a unidade farmacêutica, liderada pela injeção para esclerose múltipla Ocrevus, cuja receita cresceu 9% em moedas constantes, atingindo 1,84 bilhão de francos.

items.title: SAP clients increasingly worry about AI models' origin, CFO says
items.author: Leo Marchandon
items.creator: Leo Marchandon
items.summary: Customers are increasingly asking where the AI inside their business software was built, SAP's finance chief told Reuters on Thursday, with export controls and Europe's sovereignty debate now shaping decisions once made on price and performance alone.
items.body:
Customers are increasingly asking where the AI inside their business software was built, SAP's (SAPG.DE) finance chief told Reuters on Thursday, with export controls and Europe's sovereignty debate now shaping decisions once made on price and performance alone.
"Could data used by that model be channelled out to end up in places where it shouldn't end up?" Dominik Asam said in the interview, describing a client question SAP regularly hears. It has become an art form to understand companies' precise requirements over technology governance when juggling several AI models, he added.
SAP, Europe's most valuable tech company, embeds more than 70 models from various providers into its software that runs accounting and supply chains at many of the world's largest companies, a strategic choice to be agnostic on the market rather than internally build its own models.
But for clients, where the AI comes from matters. A US customer may not accept components developed with Chinese models, while others' back-office work, including SAP's own, can run on open-weight software "from wherever it comes from", Asam said.
"If you're a Department of Defense of a large nation, you will think about that differently as opposed to a mom-and-pop shop."
[USN:S8N3UV03C TEXT:"European debate"] over a possible "kill switch" in US cloud infrastructure has also fed the market for sovereign alternatives, Asam said. SAP has recently signed deals with governments and defence contractors, and prefers access to models from every region, including Europe and Canada, so it can offer a flexible portfolio to such clients, he said.
Asked whether this week's [USN:FWN4661WD TEXT:"PHP vulnerability"] disclosures had touched SAP, Asam said the company was using frontier AI models to attack and test its own products before anyone else could do it.
"Anyone who says I don't have any vulnerabilities would lie to you," he said, while declining to comment on findings of such screenings.

items.title: Nasdaq futures drop over 1% as AI worries resurface, oil climbs
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Nasdaq futures slid more than 1% on Thursday as high-growth stocks faced renewed pressure after earnings from Tesla and Meta Platforms did little to allay concerns over AI spending, while a rebound in oil prices further dampened sentiment.
items.body:
Nasdaq futures slid more than 1% on Thursday as high-growth stocks faced renewed pressure after earnings from Tesla and Meta Platforms did little to allay concerns over AI spending, while a rebound in oil prices further dampened sentiment.
The weakness follows a strong session on Wednesday when the tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street higher as robust results from SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Super Micro (SMCI.O) rekindled optimism around AI-linked stocks.
SpaceX dropped 2.3% and Super Micro fell 4.7% in premarket trading on Thursday as investors shifted their focus from earnings to the mounting cost of the AI buildout.
Tesla (TSLA.O) fell 5.3% after the [USN:L4N4671SD TEXT:"electric-vehicle maker"] cut its annual capital expenditure forecast, raising questions about the pace of its AI and robotics expansion.
Meta's (META.O) shares slipped 1.9% after the social media giant introduced new non-voting shares to help fund its costly AI push, reviving investor scrutiny of the substantial capital required to stay competitive in the race.
The 'Magnificent 7' stocks were also down, with Amazon.com (AMZN.O) declining 1.6% and Nvidia (NVDA.O) down 2.4%.
Chip stocks dropped, too. Intel (INTC.O) was down 5.1%, while AMD (AMD.O) , Qualcomm (QCOM.O) , Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) , Broadcom (AVGO.O) and Micron Technology (MU.O) slipped between 2.9% and 5.3%.
At 04:56 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were down 367 points, or 0.69%, S&P 500 E-minis were down 85.5 points, or 1.1%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 578.5 points, or 1.93%.
Brent crude climbed more than 3% to $112 a barrel, near a five-month high, after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked fears of supply disruptions and a wider Middle East conflict.
A flight to safety pushed the 10-year yield down to around 5.085%.
Bitcoin fell 3.4%, reflecting a broader risk-off mood as investors sought safer-haven assets.
Later in the day, earnings from Spotify (SPOT.N) , Blackstone (BX.N) , American Airlines (AAL.O) and Honeywell International (HON.O) are expected to offer a broader read on corporate performance across sectors.
IBM (IBM.N) fell 5.7% even after raising annual software revenue forecast and reporting [USN:L4N4671T3 TEXT:"third-quarter"] ahead of Wall Street expectations.

items.title: Shark nicknamed 'Bukangi' foils rescue attempts, returns to South Korean canal
items.author: Maggie Grether, Hyun Yi
items.creator: Maggie Grether, Hyun Yi
items.summary: A shark that South Korean authorities spent hours guiding into the open sea has swum back into a canal in the port city of Busan, eluding a net that was meant to prevent her return.
items.body:
A shark that South Korean authorities spent hours guiding into the open sea has swum back into a canal in the port city of Busan, eluding a net that was meant to prevent her return.
The 3-meter-long (10-foot) shark, nicknamed "Bukangi" after the Korean name for Busan's North Port, has become a viral sensation since she was spotted in the canal late last month, attracting 1.6 million visitors, according to the Busan Infrastructure Corporation.
Authorities have so far made three attempts to encourage her to return to the open sea, the latest of which was on Wednesday involving floating platforms, nets, and divers.
On Wednesday, after a month in the canal, Bukangi was successfully guided back into the open sea, according to the oceans ministry.
But on Thursday, the ministry said that the shark had swum under one of the nets installed in the canal to be caught between the outer net and an inner net installed 30 to 40 meters deeper into the waterway.
Officials have opened the outer net and reinforced barriers to prevent the shark from retreating further, in hopes that Bukangi would move out into the open water, they said.
Experts said no further efforts to guide Bukangi out to the open sea are necessary, as the shark’s condition is stable. Authorities will continue to monitor her condition, the ministry added.
South Korea's National Institute of Fisheries Science has identified Bukangi as a female dusky shark.
The shark's prolonged stay has raised environmental concerns, with experts pointing to warming ocean temperatures as the cause of more frequent shark sightings along South Korea's east coast. Dusky sharks are classified as endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.
items.raw_description: A shark that South Korean authorities spent hours guiding into the open sea has swum back into a canal in the port city of Busan, eluding a net that was meant to prevent her return.

items.title: マクロスコープ：27年春闘、芳野会長「底上げ余地まだ」　専門家は5％の着地予想
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Kentaro Sugiyama　Makiko Yamazaki

［東京　２２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Kentaro Sugiyama　Makiko Yamazaki

［東京　２２日　ロイター］ - ２０２７年春闘の基本構想で連合は賃上げ率（定期昇給込み）を「６％中心、５％以上」とし、従来より高い数値目標を設定した。これまで３年連続で５％超の賃上げを実現してきたが、芳野友子会長は全体の底上げが足りないと主張する。一方、賃金情勢に詳しいエコノミストの間では５％前後で着地するとの見方が多い。

連合は２２日、「６％中心、５％以上」とする基本構想を発表した。過去３年にわたり目標に掲げた「５％以上」を実現してきたことを踏まえ、より高い目標を設定する必要があると判断した。一方、目標達成に至っていない産業別組織や単組は、引き続き５％以上が目標になるとした。

連合は２４年春闘で「５％以上」を賃上げ目標の目安とし、２５年は「その実現を目指す」、２６年は「その実現にこだわる」と段階的に表現を強めてきた。

妥結結果は２４年が５．１０％、２５年が５．２５％、２６年が５．０１％と３年連続で５％台を確保したが、企業規模間や産業別の格差が課題となっている。２７年も大企業・製造業が相場形成をけん引する構図は続くとみられる中、中小企業や非製造業への賃上げの波及が焦点となる。

同日会見した芳野会長は「５％以上の賃上げ率となった加盟組合の比率はいまだ５割に届いていない。全体の底上げの余地は、まだまだある」と語った。

連合の基本構想では、単年度の賃上げ目標に加え、２０３０年をめどに現行水準から１５％程度引き上げる中期目標も新たに設定した。

海外主要国で賃金が年１─２％ずつ上昇していることを踏まえ、「少なくとも日本全体の実質賃金の改善スピードを１％以上で維持」しつつ、中期的に日本全体の生産性を引き上げることでさらに加速する必要があると指摘した。

実際の賃上げ率は例年、要求水準を下回る。連合は６％を中心水準として掲げたが、民間エコノミストの間では５％前後で着地するとの見方が多い。

伊藤忠総研の高野蒼太・副主任研究員は、構造的な人手不足が続く中、賃上げ率が大きく下振れするリスクは高くないと指摘。ただ、昨年に比べて物価上昇率が鈍化していることなどから「４％台後半に着地する可能性が高い」と話す。

みずほ総合研究所の服部直樹チーフ日本経済エコノミストは、２７年の賃上げ率を定昇込みで５％ちょうどと予想する。企業収益や雇用環境を踏まえれば、５％前後の賃上げは十分実現可能だとみる。

日銀は持続的・安定的な２％の物価目標実現に向け、賃金と物価の好循環を重視している。連合は年内に正式な２７年春闘方針を決定し、その後、各産業別組織や単組が要求内容をまとめる。２７年の春闘の動向は、今後の金融政策運営を占う上でも重要な材料となる。
